subject.name: Linear Algebra
subject.description: First-year linear algebra for engineering: vectors and geometry, systems of equations, matrices and determinants, vector spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues, orthogonality and least squares, and the diagonalization theory that underpins second-year methods. University-independent — everything expected before second year.

depth_levels.awareness: Know it exists and recognize it
depth_levels.procedural: Apply it mechanically to standard problems
depth_levels.fluency: Combine it with other tools in multi-step problems
depth_levels.proof: State it precisely and prove or derive it

topics.name: Vectors and Vector Geometry
topics.description: The geometric starting point: vectors in the plane and space, the operations on them, and the geometry of lines and planes.

subtopics.name: Vectors in R² and R³: notation and geometric meaning
subtopics.description: Points versus vectors, components, position vectors, and the arrow picture.

subtopics.name: Vector addition, subtraction, and scalar multiplication
subtopics.description: The parallelogram and triangle rules; scaling and negation of vectors.

subtopics.name: Linear combinations of vectors
subtopics.description: Building vectors from others; the geometric meaning of a linear combination.

subtopics.name: Vector magnitude (norm) and unit vectors
subtopics.description: Length of a vector, normalizing to a unit vector, standard basis vectors i, j, k.

subtopics.name: The dot (scalar) product and its properties
subtopics.description: Definition, algebraic properties, and the link to length and orthogonality.

subtopics.name: Angle between vectors and vector projection
subtopics.description: cosθ from the dot product; scalar and vector projections; work as a dot product.

subtopics.name: The cross product in R³
subtopics.description: Definition, right-hand rule, magnitude as area, and algebraic properties.

subtopics.name: Scalar and vector triple products
subtopics.description: The scalar triple product as a volume; coplanarity tests.

subtopics.name: Lines and planes in R³: vector, parametric, and normal forms
subtopics.description: Direction vectors, normal vectors, and converting between equation forms.

subtopics.name: Distances between points, lines, and planes
subtopics.description: Point-to-line and point-to-plane distances via projection and normals.

subtopics.name: Vectors in Rⁿ: generalizing beyond three dimensions
subtopics.description: n-tuples, the standard operations, dot product and norm in Rⁿ.

topics.name: Systems of Linear Equations
topics.description: The central computational engine of the course: solving systems by elimination and understanding the structure of their solution sets.

subtopics.name: Linear equations and their solution sets
subtopics.description: What makes an equation linear; solutions as intersections.

subtopics.name: Geometric interpretation of systems (intersecting lines and planes)
subtopics.description: Two/three-variable systems as intersections; the three solution outcomes geometrically.

subtopics.name: Representing systems with augmented matrices
subtopics.description: Coefficient and augmented matrices; the three elementary row operations.

subtopics.name: Gaussian elimination and row echelon form
subtopics.description: Forward elimination to echelon form; back substitution; pivots.

subtopics.name: Gauss–Jordan elimination and reduced row echelon form
subtopics.description: Full reduction to RREF; uniqueness of the reduced form.

subtopics.name: Consistency and the number of solutions (unique, none, infinitely many)
subtopics.description: Reading solvability off an echelon form; pivot versus free columns.

subtopics.name: Free variables and parametric solution descriptions
subtopics.description: Writing the general solution with parameters; solution sets as lines/planes.

subtopics.name: Homogeneous systems and their solution structure
subtopics.description: The trivial solution, nontrivial solutions, and the solution space.

subtopics.name: Rank of a system and the Rouché–Capelli criterion
subtopics.description: Rank of coefficient vs augmented matrix; deciding consistency and dimension of solutions.

subtopics.name: Applications: networks, balancing equations, and circuit currents
subtopics.description: Modelling flows, chemical equations, and Kirchhoff's laws as linear systems.

topics.name: Matrices and Matrix Algebra
topics.description: Matrices as objects in their own right: the operations, the inverse, and the factorizations that make computation possible.

subtopics.name: Matrix notation, size, and entries
subtopics.description: Rows, columns, dimensions, and indexing conventions.

subtopics.name: Matrix addition and scalar multiplication
subtopics.description: Entrywise operations and their algebraic rules.

subtopics.name: Matrix multiplication and its interpretation
subtopics.description: Row-by-column definition; multiplication as composition and as linear combinations of columns.

subtopics.name: Algebraic properties of matrix operations (and non-commutativity)
subtopics.description: Associativity, distributivity, the identity, and why AB ≠ BA in general.

subtopics.name: The transpose of a matrix and its properties
subtopics.description: Definition and the rule (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ.

subtopics.name: Diagonal, triangular, symmetric, and identity matrices
subtopics.description: Named matrix families and their defining properties.

subtopics.name: The matrix equation Ax = b and its solution sets
subtopics.description: Rewriting linear systems as Ax = b; existence and uniqueness in matrix terms.

subtopics.name: The inverse of a matrix
subtopics.description: Definition, the 2×2 formula, uniqueness, and (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹.

subtopics.name: Computing inverses by Gauss–Jordan elimination
subtopics.description: The [A | I] → [I | A⁻¹] algorithm and when it fails.

subtopics.name: The invertible matrix theorem (equivalent conditions)
subtopics.description: The chain of equivalent statements characterizing an invertible square matrix.

subtopics.name: Elementary matrices and their role in row reduction
subtopics.description: Row operations as left multiplication; inverses of elementary matrices.

subtopics.name: LU factorization of a matrix
subtopics.description: Factoring A = LU from elimination and solving systems with it.

subtopics.name: Block (partitioned) matrices
subtopics.description: Multiplying and inverting matrices by blocks.

topics.name: Determinants
topics.description: A single number that captures invertibility, volume scaling, and orientation, with the rules for computing and using it.

subtopics.name: The determinant of 2×2 and 3×3 matrices
subtopics.description: The 2×2 formula and the rule of Sarrus for 3×3.

subtopics.name: Cofactor (Laplace) expansion for n×n determinants
subtopics.description: Minors, cofactors, and expansion along any row or column.

subtopics.name: Evaluating determinants using row operations
subtopics.description: How each elementary operation changes the determinant; triangular shortcut.

subtopics.name: Properties of determinants
subtopics.description: Effect of transpose, zero rows, repeated rows, and linearity in a row.

subtopics.name: The determinant of a product and of an inverse
subtopics.description: det(AB) = det(A)det(B) and det(A⁻¹) = 1/det(A).

subtopics.name: Determinants and invertibility
subtopics.description: A is invertible ⇔ det(A) ≠ 0; adding det to the invertible matrix theorem.

subtopics.name: The adjugate and the inverse via cofactors
subtopics.description: The cofactor (adjugate) matrix and the formula A⁻¹ = adj(A)/det(A).

subtopics.name: Cramer's rule
subtopics.description: Solving square systems by ratios of determinants; when it is (im)practical.

subtopics.name: Determinants as area and volume; orientation
subtopics.description: |det| as the scaling factor for area/volume; sign as orientation.

topics.name: Vector Spaces and Subspaces
topics.description: The abstraction that unifies the course: spaces, subspaces, span, independence, basis, dimension, and the fundamental subspaces of a matrix.

subtopics.name: Vector spaces: the defining axioms
subtopics.description: The ten axioms; verifying whether a given set with operations is a vector space.

subtopics.name: Examples of vector spaces (Rⁿ, matrices, polynomials, functions)
subtopics.description: Recognizing familiar objects as vector spaces beyond arrows in space.

subtopics.name: Subspaces and the subspace test
subtopics.description: Closure under addition and scaling; testing whether a subset is a subspace.

subtopics.name: The span of a set of vectors
subtopics.description: Spanning sets; span as the smallest subspace containing a set.

subtopics.name: Column space, row space, and null space of a matrix
subtopics.description: The fundamental subspaces and how row reduction reveals them.

subtopics.name: Linear independence and dependence
subtopics.description: Definition, the dependence relation, and geometric meaning.

subtopics.name: Testing independence via row reduction and determinants
subtopics.description: Deciding independence of vectors using RREF or the determinant.

subtopics.name: Basis of a vector space
subtopics.description: Independent spanning sets; standard and non-standard bases.

subtopics.name: Dimension and its invariance
subtopics.description: All bases have the same size; dimensions of common spaces and subspaces.

subtopics.name: Coordinates relative to a basis
subtopics.description: Coordinate vectors and the isomorphism to Rⁿ.

subtopics.name: Rank, nullity, and the rank–nullity theorem
subtopics.description: Dimensions of column and null spaces and the relation rank + nullity = n.

subtopics.name: Change of basis and transition matrices
subtopics.description: Converting coordinates between bases; the change-of-basis matrix and its inverse.

topics.name: Linear Transformations
topics.description: Functions that respect vector-space structure, their matrices, and what kernel and image reveal about them.

subtopics.name: Linear transformations: definition and examples
subtopics.description: Additivity and homogeneity; recognizing linear versus nonlinear maps.

subtopics.name: The standard matrix of a linear transformation
subtopics.description: Building the matrix from images of basis vectors; every linear map on Rⁿ is a matrix.

subtopics.name: Geometric transformations of the plane (rotation, reflection, scaling, shear)
subtopics.description: Standard matrices for common 2D transformations and their composition.

subtopics.name: Kernel (null space) and image (range) of a transformation
subtopics.description: Defining and computing the kernel and image; relation to matrix subspaces.

subtopics.name: One-to-one and onto transformations
subtopics.description: Characterizing injectivity via the kernel and surjectivity via the image.

subtopics.name: Composition of transformations and matrix products
subtopics.description: Composition corresponds to multiplying standard matrices.

subtopics.name: Invertible transformations and their matrices
subtopics.description: When a transformation is invertible; the inverse map's matrix.

subtopics.name: Matrix of a transformation relative to general bases
subtopics.description: Representing a transformation in arbitrary input/output bases.

topics.name: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
topics.description: The directions a matrix merely stretches, the characteristic equation that finds them, and the invariants of similar matrices.

subtopics.name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors: definition and meaning
subtopics.description: Av = λv; the geometric picture of invariant directions.

subtopics.name: The characteristic equation and characteristic polynomial
subtopics.description: det(A − λI) = 0; finding eigenvalues as its roots.

subtopics.name: Computing eigenvectors and eigenspaces
subtopics.description: Solving (A − λI)v = 0 for each eigenvalue; the eigenspace as a null space.

subtopics.name: Properties of eigenvalues (trace, determinant, powers)
subtopics.description: Sum and product of eigenvalues; eigenvalues of Aᵏ and A⁻¹.

subtopics.name: Algebraic and geometric multiplicity
subtopics.description: Counting eigenvalues with multiplicity; when geometric < algebraic.

subtopics.name: Complex eigenvalues and eigenvectors
subtopics.description: Real matrices with complex spectra; conjugate pairs and rotation blocks.

subtopics.name: Similar matrices and their shared invariants
subtopics.description: B = P⁻¹AP; similarity preserves eigenvalues, trace, and determinant.

topics.name: Diagonalization
topics.description: Turning a matrix into a diagonal one in a new basis, and why that makes powers, dynamics, and differential equations easy.

subtopics.name: Diagonalization: when a matrix is diagonalizable
subtopics.description: The eigenbasis condition; the criterion in terms of multiplicities.

subtopics.name: Diagonalizing a matrix in practice
subtopics.description: Assembling P from eigenvectors and D from eigenvalues; A = PDP⁻¹.

subtopics.name: Using diagonalization to compute matrix powers
subtopics.description: Aᵏ = PDᵏP⁻¹ and evaluating matrix polynomials.

subtopics.name: Applications: difference equations and discrete dynamical systems
subtopics.description: Long-term behaviour of xₖ₊₁ = Axₖ; steady states and Markov chains.

subtopics.name: The matrix exponential and systems of linear ODEs
subtopics.description: Defining e^{At} via diagonalization and solving x' = Ax.

subtopics.name: The Cayley–Hamilton theorem
subtopics.description: A matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation; using it to find inverses and powers.

topics.name: Orthogonality and Inner Product Spaces
topics.description: Length, angle, and perpendicularity in general spaces: orthonormal bases, projection, and the Gram–Schmidt process.

subtopics.name: Inner products and inner product spaces
subtopics.description: Generalizing the dot product; the axioms of an inner product.

subtopics.name: Norm, distance, and angle from an inner product
subtopics.description: Induced norm, Cauchy–Schwarz, and the triangle inequality.

subtopics.name: Orthogonal and orthonormal sets
subtopics.description: Orthogonality of vectors, orthonormal bases, and their computational advantages.

subtopics.name: Orthogonal projection onto a subspace
subtopics.description: Projecting a vector onto a line and a subspace; the best-approximation property.

subtopics.name: Orthogonal complements and the four fundamental subspaces
subtopics.description: The orthogonal complement and how the fundamental subspaces pair up.

subtopics.name: The Gram–Schmidt process
subtopics.description: Turning any basis into an orthonormal one.

subtopics.name: QR factorization
subtopics.description: Factoring A = QR from Gram–Schmidt and its uses.

subtopics.name: Orthogonal matrices and their properties
subtopics.description: QᵀQ = I; length preservation and orthonormal columns.

topics.name: Least Squares and Applications
topics.description: Best-fit solutions when a system has no exact answer — the workhorse of engineering data fitting.

subtopics.name: The least-squares problem and the normal equations
subtopics.description: Minimizing ‖Ax − b‖; deriving and solving AᵀAx = Aᵀb.

subtopics.name: Least-squares curve fitting and linear regression
subtopics.description: Fitting lines, polynomials, and models to data by least squares.

subtopics.name: Solving least squares with QR factorization
subtopics.description: Using A = QR for a numerically stable least-squares solution.

subtopics.name: Approximate solutions to inconsistent systems
subtopics.description: Interpreting the least-squares solution when no exact solution exists.

topics.name: Symmetric Matrices and Quadratic Forms
topics.description: The especially well-behaved symmetric case: orthogonal diagonalization, the spectral theorem, quadratic forms, and the SVD.

subtopics.name: Orthogonal diagonalization of symmetric matrices
subtopics.description: Symmetric matrices have orthonormal eigenbases; A = QDQᵀ.

subtopics.name: The spectral theorem for symmetric matrices
subtopics.description: Real eigenvalues, orthogonal eigenspaces, and the spectral decomposition.

subtopics.name: Quadratic forms and their matrices
subtopics.description: Writing a quadratic form as xᵀAx with A symmetric.

subtopics.name: The principal axes theorem and change of variable
subtopics.description: Eliminating cross terms by rotating to eigenvector axes; conic/quadric classification.

subtopics.name: Positive-definite matrices and classification of quadratic forms
subtopics.description: Positive/negative definite, semidefinite, and indefinite via eigenvalue signs.

subtopics.name: The singular value decomposition (introduction)
subtopics.description: A = UΣVᵀ; singular values and what the SVD reveals about any matrix.

topics.name: Complex and Numerical Linear Algebra
topics.description: The finishing tools: complex vectors and matrices, and the numerical realities of solving large systems on a computer.

subtopics.name: Complex numbers: arithmetic, modulus, and the complex plane
subtopics.description: Rectangular and polar forms, conjugates, modulus, and Euler's formula.

subtopics.name: Complex vector spaces and the complex (Hermitian) inner product
subtopics.description: Vectors over C and the conjugate-linear inner product.

subtopics.name: Hermitian and unitary matrices
subtopics.description: The complex analogues of symmetric and orthogonal matrices.

subtopics.name: Partial pivoting and numerical stability
subtopics.description: Why elimination reorders rows; roundoff and loss of significance.

subtopics.name: Condition number and ill-conditioned systems
subtopics.description: Sensitivity of solutions to small perturbations in A or b.

subtopics.name: Iterative methods for linear systems (Jacobi and Gauss–Seidel)
subtopics.description: Solving large sparse systems by iteration; convergence conditions.

subtopics.name: The power method for the dominant eigenvalue
subtopics.description: Iteratively approximating the largest eigenvalue and its eigenvector.
